target_customer: Cell and gene therapy developers that need to manufacture stem-cell-derived cells at scale
problem: Regenerative medicine cells are made by hand in cleanrooms, which is costly and does not scale to millions of patients.
business_model: Automated contract development and manufacturing (CDMO) services plus proprietary iDEM closed-system bioreactor technology

founders.name: Ali Afshar
education: Imperial College London (student when founding, per TechCrunch)
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a scientist and engineer; TechCrunch calls him the scientist.

founders.name: Ignacio Willats
education: Imperial College London (student when founding, per TechCrunch)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch calls him the events and startups guy. They met running a lab automation event at Imperial.

competitors.name: Transcriptic
competitors.what: Robotic cloud laboratory offering on-demand biology experiments, a general lab automation adjacent player
competitors.traction_then: Roughly 40 staff and pharma customers per a 2016 report; adjacent rather than direct cell manufacturing

technical_complexity.rationale: Closed-system robotic differentiation of stem cells over weeks combines hardware, biology and process control, hard for a student founded team in 2018.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware plus validated processes embedded in clinical manufacturing creates switching costs once partners tech-transfer, but little was proven in 2018.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found through 2025; the company remained independent and launched its own CDMO in Oct 2025.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in Aug 2018 reported promising prospects including an unnamed gene therapy company, and big pharma was investing heavily in lab automation; cultivated meat was named as another use.

branding.domain_note: Now uses mytos.bio; earlier domain history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical B2B biomanufacturing language with quantified claims

rebrands.why: TechCrunch says the name was changed to reflect the narrowed cell culture focus
Reason not stated; dates from UK Companies House as summarized in search results

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand itself; B2B brand with limited visible community. Two renames show the early name did not stick.

pivots.why: Client interest concentrated in cell culture

pivots.to: Automated CDMO for stem-cell derived therapies
pivots.why: Company launched a CDMO service model; reason not stated

outcome_analysis: Mytos is still active after several renames and a shift from general lab automation to cell manufacturing. It raised a 19M Series A in late 2023 and signed partners such as Aspen Neuroscience in 2025. It has not exited and no shutdown cause applies; the main risk is slow cell therapy demand, with the CDMO launch in October 2025 an attempt to capture more value.
notes: Series A of 19M reported by multiple outlets (Endpoints, Biopharma Reporter, Forbes); investor list from a search summary, not opened (Endpoints, Medical Design pages returned 403). CB Insights lists a 2018 seed with no amount; not recorded. Rebrand dates from Companies House as summarized in a search result. Competitor Transcriptic is adjacent. Seedtable totals of 38M or 57M look unreliable.
